data.narrative:
1X Technologies is a Series B-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $123.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine firms: eight private robotics and automation players (including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Nimble Robotics) and one public company. The private peer set spans Series B through Series C stages.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The stage-progression approach, anchoring to the company's $123.5M total raised as a $3.0B proxy and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $5.7B. The peer-median method examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), Hadrian ($1.6B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B)—yielding a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B to $1.8B.

Triangulating these methods produces a low estimate of $1.4B, median of $3.7B, and high of $6.6B. The wide dispersion reflects material tension between recent-stage peers trading at $1.0B–$1.8B valuations and the higher implied value from stage-based progression. Key uncertainties include the comparability of raised capital to true pre-money valuation and heterogeneity in business models and maturity across the peer set. The peer-median approach likely anchors to more recent market-tested prices, while stage progression may overweight historical capital efficiency.
